title: Iran denies Trump’s claim of talks; Israeli strikes on Gaza kill over 30 since Friday “deal”; Cuba’s electricity collapses again
author: Drop Site News
content:
**Monday, August 3, 2026 -**_** ** President Donald Trump says U.S.-Iran talks
will resume Monday; Tehran says no negotiations underway. Iran strikes Kuwait.
NYT: U.S. dropped a 2,000-pound bomb on family in Qeshm. Iran says it is near
agreement for Hormuz control. Saudi Crown Prince notes Saudi concern about
strikes on call with Trump. Iran says several U.S. allies will not participate
in future U.S. strikes. Two more executed in Iran. Ansarallah will not charge
for Bab Al-Mandab transit, officials say. Two Saudi oil tankers transit Bab
Al-Mandab despite Ansarallah blockade. Israel kills 34 Palestinians, wounds
134 since Gaza deal announcement. UN: 67% of Gaza faces food insecurity, 10%
nears famine. Report: Israeli forces, settlers carried out 2,256 attacks in
West Bank in July. Israel says it will not withdraw from Gaza despite
agreement. Israeli court freezes Itamar Ben Gvir's plan for crocodiles in
prison moat over animal rights concerns. Israeli phosphorus attacks hit
southern Lebanon despite ceasefire. Lebanon-Israel talks progressing while
blast wounds five Lebanese soldiers. Major primary contests set for Michigan,
Missouri, Washington state, Kansas, Virginia. Rep. Haley Stevens features
pastor with anti-LGBTQ, Islamophobic history in Michigan Senate ad. Justice
Department scraps parts of Trump's IRS deal to save Todd Blanche's Attorney
General confirmation. Sen. Bernie Moreno calls former son-in-law Rep. Max
Miller "unfit for office." Education Secretary Linda McMahon asks universities
to commit to reforms by end of 2026. Author of DNC autopsy says party buried
chapter questioning Joe Biden's 2024 run. Senate appropriators unveil stopgap
bill to avert shutdown. Drone strikes Russian Black Sea resort, killing six.
Suicide bombing kills 17 outside police station in northwest Pakistan. Cuban
electricity grid collapses again. Trump's shadow envoy in Venezuela is out.
Taiwan defense chief states that U.S. military ties are "far closer" than
publicly understood. Sudanese army drone strike on a community court in Darfur
kills at least 35. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claims Cuba is operating a
vast espionage and influence network inside the United States. Turkey and Iraq
sign one-year deal to keep Iraqi crude flowing to the Mediterranean, bypassing
the Gulf. U.S. Treasury steps in to help Japan's yen._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **Trump says U.S.-Iran talks will resume Monday; Tehran says no negotiations underway:** President Donald Trump [announced](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2084077388892119139) that renewed diplomatic negotiations with Iran would begin on Monday afternoon, claiming he had shelved plans for what he had previously described as "biggest attack since World War II."

    * Speaking to reporters onboard Air Force One, President Trump stated that the impending military operation was aborted at the last minute following direct appeals from key Middle Eastern allies, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE.

    * He also told reporters that the talks would address the Strait of Hormuz and the "denuclearization of Iran."

    * Iran's Foreign Ministry [said](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/246733/Understanding-with-Oman-not-mean-reopening-Strait-of-Hormuz) Monday that Tehran is "not holding any negotiations with the United States at present," stressing that ongoing talks are exclusively with Oman and focused on reaching "an understanding on the safe passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Mehr News Agency reported.

    * At a weekly press briefing, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said that Iran "has never been the first party to violate any understanding," adding that "the ball has been in the U.S. court for quite some time" after Washington announced on July 7 that it would no longer honor its commitments under the June 17 memorandum of understanding.

  * **Iran strikes Kuwait:** Iran [launched](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083470497178603948) strikes toward Kuwait overnight Friday, Kuwait's Defense Ministry reported, claiming that it disabled the wave of attacks.

    * The ministry accused Iran of targeting several vital sites, including a government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian vehicles belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island.

  * **U.S. begins to withdraw from Erbil:** The U.S. began withdrawing its remaining forces and heavy equipment from the military compound near Erbil airport on Saturday, including all Patriot air-defense batteries, as Washington approaches a September 30 deadline for a full troop pullout from Iraq, Al-Monitor reports.

    * Sources said U.S. interceptors had stopped at least 95% of strikes targeting Erbil airport, leaving Kurdish officials concerned that the region is now more exposed. Remaining U.S. special forces may continue operating from smaller, low-profile locations in the country, an analyst said.

  * **NYT: U.S. dropped a 2,000-pound bomb on family in Qeshm:** Video, satellite imagery, and weapons analysis indicate the U.S. dropped a 2,000-pound bomb on a family home in a densely populated residential neighborhood on Iran's Qeshm Island overnight Thursday, The New York Times [reported](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083605076195545185) on Saturday.

    * The strike killed a husband, wife, and their 2-year-old son. Two other children, now orphaned, were pulled alive from the rubble.

  * **Iranian FM says Iran will respond "decisively" to attacks:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [warned](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083646576732365116) on Saturday that Iran is prepared to respond "decisively" to any U.S. aggression, according to the Iranian state-affiliated outlet Tasnim News.

    * Araghchi held calls on Saturday with Pakistan Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan, and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan to discuss the "destabilizing consequences" of U.S. actions in the region.

  * **Iran announces that it is near agreement for Hormuz control:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [said](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083989370571288963) on Sunday that talks with Oman over a mechanism to govern the strait are "nearing completion and in their final stages," according to state news agency IRNA.

    * Iran has previously demanded control over both of the northern and southern routes that transit the Strait, and has rejected a proposal from Oman and the U.S. that would give it control of only one.

    * Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday that negotiations with Oman are focused on establishing a single, intermediate two-way shipping corridor to temporarily replace the existing northern and southern routes until a permanent Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) is agreed upon.

  * **MBS notes Saudi concern about strikes on call with Trump:** Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman [reportedly urged](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/01/saudi-crown-prince-trump-iran-attacks) Trump to de-escalate and hold off on infrastructure strikes against Iran, asking for "clarity" on Trump's war plans.

    * The Wall Street Journal, however, reported on Sunday that the UAE [lobbied](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083940865895002117) President Trump to take "more decisive action" against Iran, arguing that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps would not compromise unless Washington escalated, took control of the Strait of Hormuz and potentially considered ground operations, the report says.

  * **Iran says several countries tell its FM they will not participate in future U.S. strikes:** A spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry [announced](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083996631616164130) on Sunday that "in the past 24 hours," representatives from the U.K., Bulgaria, and Ukraine had contacted the FM and said that they would not play any role in potential U.S. attacks on Iran.

    * The FM noted in the same statement that any country that did participate in these strikes would "face Iran's legitimate defense," and noted that this included countries who "provided bases or military and logistical facilities" to the U.S.

  * **Two more executed in Iran:** Iran executed two men on Monday convicted on charges of spying for Israel during both the June 2025 war and the ongoing conflict, according to the state affiliated news agency Mizan. The two men were identified as Omid Behzad and Pouria Safvat.

    * Last week, Iran publicly hanged two men convicted of killing police officers during mass anti-government protests in January. At least 60 others convicted on charges related to the protests are at risk of execution, [according](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2026/07/iran-end-escalating-campaign-of-arbitrary-executions-and-death-sentences-against-protesters/) to Amnesty International.

    * "The Iranian authorities are unleashing a horrifying wave of executions and death sentences to punish and suppress dissent and project an image of strength and absolute control in the wake of the January popular uprising and amid ongoing attacks by U.S. and Israeli forces," Heba Morayef, Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa at Amnesty International, said in a statement.

# Yemen

  * **Ansarallah will not charge for Bab Al-Mandab transit, officials say:** Ansarallah's maritime coordination body [denied](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083487438895194532) that it had plans to charge commercial vessels for passing through Bab Al-Mandab, and affirmed that transit through the waterway would remain free, The New Arab reported on Saturday.

    * The body said the "safe transit service" it has devised in light of its embargo on Saudi shipping is voluntary and free.

    * Officials warned shipping companies not to make payments to or share information with unauthorized parties.

  * **Two Saudi oil tankers transit Bab Al-Mandab despite Ansarallah blockade:** Shipping data showed that two tankers carrying Saudi crude transited the Bab Al-Mandab Strait over the weekend despite Ansarallah's declared maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia since July 20. According to Kpler data, the Suezmax tanker Lesbos, carrying about 1 million barrels of Saudi crude, and the VLCC DHT Vibhav, carrying 2 million barrels, both left the Red Sea with their Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders switched off.

# Palestine

  * **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, 19 Palestinians were killed--18 in new attacks and one succumbing to wounds--and 35 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

    * The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,375 killed, with 174,220 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,250 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,110, while 804 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.

  * **Israel kills 34 Palestinians, wounds 134 since Gaza deal announcement:** Since Trump's Friday announcement of a "historic agreement" and Hamas's acceptance of phase two of the Gaza ceasefire deal, conditioned on Israeli compliance, Israeli attacks have killed at least 34 Palestinians and wounded 134 others across the Strip, according to Gaza's Ministry of Health.

    * An Israeli drone [targeted](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173088) the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City Saturday, killing two Palestinians and wounding several others, WAFA reported. An attack later on Saturday killed another Palestinian in the Sabra neighborhood.

    * An Israeli drone strike on the Al-Mawasi area, near Khan Younis, [killed](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083642549802021373) one Palestinian and injured others Saturday.

    * Also on Saturday, an Israeli drone struck Deir Al-Balah and [killed](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083642549802021373) four Palestinians, wounding others.

    * **Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah** filed a report from an attack near Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital in Deir Al-Balah, which destroyed two central medicine warehouses, including critical equipment for kidney dialysis, and nearby tents sheltering displaced families. One resident asked, "What did we do to deserve this?" and noted that residents believed that the latest deal announced by Trump would improve their situation. "What did we do wrong?" she asked. "What did we do to deserve this, us and the dialysis patients? Who among us is guilty?" **The full dispatch is available[ here](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083671037699404047).**

    * On Sunday, an Israeli [strike](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173113) on an apartment building in Gaza City killed two Palestinians, including a child, and wounded several others.

    * A separate Israeli airstrike west of Khan Younis [killed](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083712130931462307) three members of a family, including a child. Another Israeli attack on Sunday afternoon in the area wounded five, three of whom were children.

    * An Israeli attack on Sunday [targeted](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083992485160702166) an apartment building in Gaza City, killing an entire family of four, including a 5-year-old and an unborn baby that was reportedly ripped from its mother's body by the force of the blast.

    * Hamas issued a statement [condemning](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083975080493883605) the attacks on Sunday, noting that "criminal and frenzied bombardment" had killed 18 Palestinians since dawn and accusing Israel of deliberately escalating to sabotage the recently announced ceasefire agreement.

    * Nickolay Mladenov, who leads the U.S.-backed "Board of Peace," [responded](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2084010720715305200) to the Israeli strikes by noting that the attacks had killed civilians and "destroyed medical supplies that people depend on," without naming or condemning Israel.

    * Senior Hamas official Basem Naim criticized the ongoing Israeli attacks: "At a time when Hamas demonstrated considerable flexibility and a high degree of responsibility by agreeing to the roadmap presented by the Board of Peace for the transition to the second phase of the Gaza War Termination Agreement, the Israeli occupation significantly escalated its targeting of civilians," he said in a statement. "Its attacks have not ceased since the understandings were announced."

  * **UN: 67% of Gaza faces food insecurity, 10% nears famine:** The head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the occupied Palestinian territory, Justin Brady, [warned](https://www.aljazeera.net/news/2026/8/3/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A9-10-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%B3%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%BA%D8%B2%D8%A9-%D9%8A%D9%82%D8%AA%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%86) Monday that Gaza remains in a food emergency and is at risk of reaching Phase 5 of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), the threshold for an official famine declaration, Al Jazeera reported.

  * **Report: Israeli forces, settlers carried out 2,256 attacks in West Bank in July:** Israeli forces and settlers [carried out](https://www.cwrc.ps/page-4809-ar.html) 2,256 attacks against Palestinians, their land, and property across the occupied West Bank in July, according to the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. Israeli forces were responsible for 1,458 attacks and settlers for 798, the group said, describing the violence as a coordinated campaign in which the military provides "protection and support" for settler attacks.

    * Settlers killed seven Palestinians in Nablus and Ramallah, uprooted, damaged, or poisoned 5,027 trees, damaged property in 440 incidents, and attempted to establish 29 new settlement outposts.

    * Israeli authorities issued 33 military orders targeting more than 830 dunams (~205,000 acres) of Palestinian land and carried out 80 demolition operations, destroying 165 structures.

  * **Israel continues its attacks in the occupied West Bank:**

    * **Ramallah:** Israeli settlers beat and injured a Palestinian farmer and his wife in Beitillu on Saturday; footage published later showed bandages on the couple's arms and legs.**** Israeli forces beat and pepper-sprayed at least three Palestinians, according to WAFA. A 19-year-old Palestinian was seriously wounded on Sunday after Israeli forces shot him in the thigh during a raid at the entrance to Jalazone refugee camp. Also in al-Mughayyir, an Israeli soldier on leave was arrested for allegedly taking part in the murder of a 10-year-old at a sheep farm outside of the town, according to Israel's Kan Media.

    * **Nablus:** Israeli forces issued a demolition order on Saturday for the family home of Faroukh Ramadan, the resident of Tal who defended himself by seizing the weapon of an Israeli settler who was pointing the gun at him, opening fire and killing the settler on July 24. Israeli [settlers](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173112) cut and damaged electrical poles in Madama, south of Nablus, on Sunday, WAFA reported, leaving residents without electricity. Israeli forces also conducted raids east of Nablus, [breaking into](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173114) several homes before dawn and detaining at least two residents.

    * **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [ordered](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/8/3/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B5%D8%B9%D9%91%D8%AF-%D8%B9%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%87-%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%82-%D9%85%D8%AE%D9%8A%D9%85-%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%B4%D9%85%D8%B3-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AC%D8%A8%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A5%D8%AE%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%84%D9%87%D9%85-151560) residents of the Jabal Al-Salihin area east of Nur Shams refugee camp Monday to evacuate their homes, citing planned military operations and possible explosions. The military also deployed bulldozers.

    * **Jenin:** Israeli settlers [destroyed](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173107) part of a tobacco crop in the plain of Arraba on Saturday evening, WAFA reported, noting that settlers also hurled stones at Palestinian vehicles at a road leading into the village.

    * **Hebron:** Israeli settlers [carried](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173108) out similar attacks in Idhna, throwing stones at cars while receiving protection from the Israeli military.**** Israeli forces [detained](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/173096) 11 Palestinians working the fields in the village of Khashem al-Daraj, near Yatta, on Saturday.

    * **Occupied East Jerusalem:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/8/3/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A7-%D9%84%D8%B4%D8%A4%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B3-%D8%AA%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%B1%D9%85%D9%86-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%AF%D8%B3-151562) the Armenian Church in the Old City on Sunday, throwing stones and collectively spitting at its entrance, according to WAFA.

  * **Israel agreed to halt attacks, Palestinian close to Kushner claims:** Mohammad Dahlan, the exiled former Fatah security chief in Gaza who is based in the UAE and has emerged as an influential figure in post-war planning, said Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law and lead Gaza mediator, assured him he reached an agreement with Israel to cease the assaults starting Sunday morning, as part of the roadmap deal Hamas and other factions approved this week.

    * Dahlan later deleted the portion of the tweet mentioning a U.S. agreement with Israel to end its attacks.

  * **Israel says it will not withdraw from Gaza despite agreement:** The Israeli Prime Minister's Office [issued](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083945312045891793) on Sunday its first public reaction since U.S. President Trump announced the Board of Peace agreement with Palestinian resistance factions earlier this week, saying that Israel would not withdraw from Gaza and claiming it had "serious" concerns about Hamas' continued operations in the Strip and potential to "expand" absent an Israeli presence.

    * Israel has reportedly demanded continued freedom to strike and kill Palestinians in Gaza as part of the newest agreement, according to the AP.

  * **Israeli court freezes Ben Gvir plan for crocodiles in prison moat over animal rights concerns:** An Israeli court on Sunday imposed a temporary injunction freezing a plan by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir to place crocodiles in moats around Ketziot Prison where Palestinians are held following a petition by the animal rights group Let Animals Live. The petition requested that crocodiles be reclassified as a protected species. "The claims regarding the expected harm to the crocodiles merit investigation and justify issuing an order prohibiting the transfer," Judge Avraham Rubin wrote in the ruling, [according](https://www.timesofisrael.com/court-freezes-transfer-of-crocodiles-to-prison-moat-putting-ben-gvirs-plan-on-hold/) to Times of Israel.

  * **Family of Palestinian in viral photo of Israeli soldiers mocking him appeals for urgent action:** The family of Mahmoud Al-Drimli, the Palestinian identified as the blindfolded man in a widely circulated photograph with two female Israeli soldiers smiling next to a detained Mahmoud, has [appealed](https://x.com/advil/status/2083993011453850103?s=46) for urgent international intervention to determine his fate and secure his release nearly two years after he disappeared while attempting to return to Gaza City.

    * The family called on the International Committee of the Red Cross, the United Nations, and humanitarian organizations to intervene and ensure his physical and psychological safety and work toward his release.

    * His parents previously [told](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2082912086158688659?s=46) Drop Site they have received no information about him since his disappearance in November 2024.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli phosphorus attacks hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:**

    * Overnight, Israeli warplanes struck the Ali Al-Taher heights on the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa. Forces [fired](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/555615/%D9%82%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%84-%D9%81%D9%88%D8%B3%D9%81%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%84%D8%A7-%D8%AA%D8%B3%D8%A8%D8%A8%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AF%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%83%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%86%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%B1-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%AA-%D8%AC%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%84-2) phosphorus munitions that ignited fires in olive groves and pine forests around Yaroun and the city of Bint Jbeil.

    * Israeli artillery [shelled](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/555715/%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%81-%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%B9%D9%8A-%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%81-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B3-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%A8%D9%84-2) Mais Al-Jabal in the Marjayoun district, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported, while an Israeli drone [dropped](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/555702/%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%82-%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B5%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%82%D9%86%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%A9-%D8%B5%D9%88%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A3%D9%84%D9%82%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%A7-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%8A%D9%91%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9-2) a stun grenade on a pickup truck in Al-Mansouri in Tyre district, setting it ablaze.

  * **Lebanon-Israel talks progressing while blast wounds five Lebanese soldiers:** U.S. Ambassador Michel Issa [said](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/555675/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%81%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B1%D9%83%D9%8A-%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%AB%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%85%D8%A7-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%86%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%B5%D9%84-%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%89-%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%AC-%D8%A5%D9%8A%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D8%AD%D9%85%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%8A%D9%86-2) he is encouraged by ongoing negotiations in Rome between Lebanon and Israel, according to the NNA. Issa said "significant technical work" remains to ensure civilian safety and stressed that "there is a meaningful difference between drafting an agreement on paper and implementing it responsibly."

    * Separately, the Lebanese Army [said](https://x.com/lebarmyofficial/status/2083880667100627246?s=46) five soldiers were wounded while accompanying civilians in Kafr Kila in Bint Jbeil district on Sunday. The army later said an investigation determined the explosion was caused by a "suspicious object" and was continuing to determine the remaining circumstances. Israel's military claimed the explosive device belonged to Hezbollah.

    * An Israeli officer was [wounded](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2083591542132850799) overnight Saturday during what the Israeli military described as a "close-quarters encounter" with Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon, AFP reported. The military said the officer was injured during "operational activity" in the area, without providing further details.

# U.S. News

  * **Major primary contests set for Michigan, Missouri, Washington state, Kansas, Virginia:** The most-watched race Tuesday is the Senate contest between Dr. **Abdul El-Sayed** and Rep. **Haley Stevens**. Polls show El-Sayed with a double-digit lead over Stevens despite more than $60 million being spent to boost Stevens and blunt El-Sayed. For context, $60 million is several times more than the entire Democratic National Committee has in cash on hand.
